prediction:
MECHANISM.  #13's geom.c half landed the derived edge-priority order -- for a
triangle (a, b, c) paint the edge opposite a, then opposite b, then opposite c
-- and took nine of eleven candidate classes to 100.00% of their decisive
pixels.  TFan and QStrip/TFan did not, because rewrite_triangle_fan() calls
emit_tri_pv(), which rotates the guest's provoking vertex to index 0: a fan
triangle reaches geom.c already rotated by one relative to the TRIANGLES draw
beside it, and GeomState::primitive_mode is the REWRITTEN mode, so geom.c
cannot tell them apart and cannot compensate.

THIS ARM removes that rotation in exactly the state where nothing reads index
0.  Vulkan rasterises first-vertex-provoking (nothing in vk/ enables
VK_EXT_provoking_vertex) and so does the DESKTOP GL renderer, but not the
Android one: gl/draw.c's glProvokingVertex(GL_FIRST_VERTEX_CONVENTION) sits
inside `#ifndef __ANDROID__ / glProvokingVertex not available in GLES 3.x`, so
an Android GL build keeps GLES 3.x's LAST-vertex default.  (Corrected here
after audit pass 1; earlier revisions of this prediction, the PR body and the
lane notes all said "both renderers".)  It does not reach the claim, for the
reason the edge-list argument gives below -- the rotation leaves every emitted
line's (i0, i1) pair intact, so whichever endpoint the rasteriser takes a
`flat` varying from, it takes the same one on both arms -- and every device
arm here is Vulkan in any case.  geom.c spells provoking_index as the literal
"0" only when the shade mode is FLAT -- needs_rewrite() already encodes that for PRIM_TYPE_TRIANGLES, which
it declines to rewrite at all unless the draw is flat AND last-provoking.  The
new predicate is `flat_shading || polygon_mode != POLY_MODE_LINE`, so the fan
keeps its rotation under FILL, under POINT, and under flat shading everywhere.
#13's trade is NARROWED to its one real corner -- a flat-shaded wireframe,
where the colour must win over the paint order -- not abolished.

WHY IT IS FREE ON THE WIREFRAME PATH.  geom.c splits a triangle (A, B, C) into
emit_line(B,C), emit_line(C,A), emit_line(A,B).  Rotating the triple is
therefore a pure rotation of the EDGE LIST: the multiset of ORDERED (i0, i1)
pairs is identical and only the paint order changes.  That is checked, not
argued -- see the A/B below, where the old code emits 2 0 1 / 3 0 2 / ... and
the new emits 0 1 2 / 0 2 3 / ..., the same ordered pairs in a rotated order.
So vtxFogSpecial, which glsl/common.c qualifies `flat` in EVERY shade mode but
which each emit_line() takes from that edge's OWN first endpoint rather than
from the triangle's index 0 (geom.c:438 uses `index`, chosen at geom.c:420; the widened path pins
it to the edge's own i0 at geom.c:551), is unchanged per edge.

ONE READER OF INDEX 0 DOES MOVE, AND NO LEG BELOW CAN SEE IT.  Audit pass 1
found a third reader this arm's enumeration had missed, and it is a literal
[0] rather than a provoking_index: cylWrap.  When a texture unit is in WRAP
address mode (state->cylinder_wrap[i] non-zero, from
NV_PGRAPH_TEXADDRESS0_WRAP_U/V/P/Q) geom.c:310 emits
`vtxT%d = cylWrap(v_vtxT%d[0], v_vtxT%d[index], ...)` in emit_vertex(), and
geom.c:313-314 the same `v_vtxT%d[0]` reference inside emit_vertex_fs()'s lerp -- in BOTH the
GL and the widened Vulkan paths, and independently of the shade mode.  Cylinder
wrap adjusts each vertex's texture coordinate by whole turns relative to the
INPUT PRIMITIVE'S VERTEX 0, so moving vertex 0 moves the reference.
DIRECTION: it was the rim vertex the rotation put there (v2 under
last-provoking, v1 under first), which varies from fan triangle to fan
triangle; it is now the fan HUB, one reference for the whole fan.  A rim
vertex more than half a turn from the hub but less than half a turn from its
old neighbour-reference, or the reverse, now takes a whole turn it did not
take, moving its U or V by 1.0.

This is TOLERATED, not measured, and it is stated here rather than left for a
reader to discover.  The hub is arguably the better reference -- it is what a
TRIANGLES draw of the same geometry already gets -- but this arm does not
establish that, because NOTHING IN THE REGISTERED DISC DRAWS IT: a textured
wireframe fan with WRAP addressing appears nowhere (`Shade_model`'s line-mode
prefix is kUntexturedLM, `Line width` is untextured), so every leg below is
silent on it and a clean verdict is not evidence about it either way.  If a
title regresses on textured wireframe geometry after this folds, start here.

The two remaining index-0 readers on this path are checked and do not move:
calc_triz(0, 1, 2) (a plane's gradient is rotation-invariant, so dz moves only
by rounding, and it feeds triMZ rather than coverage), and the widened path's
flat block at geom.c:534-543, which pins vtxD0/vtxD1/vtxB0/vtxB1 to a literal
[0] -- reached only under FLAT shading, where this predicate keeps the
rotation, which is a second reason the flat_shading term is load-bearing.

THE SCOPE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED.  Both revisions of prim_rewrite.c were
compiled side by side and their output diffed over every
(primitive_mode x polygon_mode x last_provoking x flat_shading x count)
